gaps.userNeed: I need to know how to turn my site into a revenue source and manage monetization tools directly from my phone so I can run a business without needing a computer.
gaps.explanation: Users view WordPress mobile as a full-fledged micro-business platform rather than just a simple content publisher. When they discover monetization options or required plugins are inaccessible or unexplained on mobile, they suffer immediate churn. Proactively guiding users on site monetization directly in the app resolves a major latent barrier for self-employed creators.

gaps.userNeed: I need complete confidence that my post edits can be undone and that my published content won't be unintentionally overwritten while I format text.
gaps.explanation: Automatic background saving creates severe friction on touchscreen devices where formatting errors and accidental taps happen constantly. Users require visible safety controls like dedicated undo history and explicit draft checkpointing to feel safe experimenting with post layouts. Without explicit state management, mobile writing causes anxiety rather than seamless productivity.
gaps.confidenceJustification: Directly supported by explicit user feedback regarding aggressive auto-saving and missing undo capabilities during rich text editing.
gaps.verdictReason: While general editor crashes are actively tracked, granular local undo history and explicit draft confirmation mechanisms are ignored in open roadmap issues.

gaps.userNeed: I need full visibility and control over my site's existing categories and templates on mobile so I can manage my site architecture seamlessly away from desktop.
gaps.explanation: Mobile managers expect structural parity with the WordPress web dashboard. When custom categories or templates are missing from the mobile workflow, users lose trust in the app for site administration and are forced back to desktop. Ensuring full taxonomy synchronization unlocks complete mobile management for established multi-category blogs.
gaps.confidenceJustification: Supported by low-star reviews highlighting missing categories and template editing limitations when attempting site management on mobile.
gaps.verdictReason: Open issues focus heavily on isolated UI bugs and tech debt, ignoring functional gaps where complex site taxonomies and templates fail to render on mobile.
